title: Working on matchmaking for my game. Still in development
author: xcantene
selftext:
This is **Hunt Protocol**, a monster-hunting card game I'm developing that can be played solo or competitively with up to 4 other Hunters.

The basic idea is that everyone is hunting the same monster at the same time, but each Hunter is building their own plan and trying to defeat it as efficiently as possible.

This video shows the first version of the **mobile multiplayer flow**, from matchmaking into the hunt itself.

Before a match, you choose your loadout: your Hunter, your deck, and three monsters you'd like to hunt.

Once everyone is ready, the Hunters contribute monsters to the target pool. A high-rank monster can also be added automatically, the pool is shuffled, and one becomes the next hunt.

When the hunt begins, every Hunter gets their own arena and plays their own cards against the same monster.

Everyone shares the same turn, so you play your actions and then continue when you're ready. You don't constantly see every card the other Hunters are playing, but you can still track their progress during the hunt, see how they're doing, and switch over to their arena if you want to watch them more closely.

The first Hunter to kill the monster sets the score to beat. Everyone else then gets one final turn to finish their own hunt and see if they can beat that score.

The winner claims the monster as a trophy and gets to choose 2 upgrades for the following hunts. The other Hunters choose 1. Those upgrades are drawn from a 20-card upgrade deck that you built as part of your loadout, so your build can develop differently every match.

A full match consists of 6 hunts, and then the next monster is revealed and everyone goes again.

There can be quite a lot of variation between matches because the Hunters, decks, selected monsters, monster decks, and upgrades can all change.

The UI is still very much in progress. I've been doing a lot of work on the animations, feedback, and general polish, so some parts are already quite different from what you see here.

What I'm most interested in right now is **how the actual competitive hunt feels from the outside**.

Does the battle look clear enough to follow? And does it still feel like you're competing against the other Hunters even though you're primarily playing inside your own arena?

You can keep track of their progress and switch over to watch their hunt, but I deliberately don't show every action from every player directly on your own screen because I don't want the battle to become overloaded.

I'm experimenting with a type of competitive monster-hunting structure I haven't really seen done this way before, so I'm curious whether that balance between **focusing on your own plan and still being aware of everyone else** comes across.

The current playable build is here if anyone wants to see where development is at:  
[https://huntprotocol.cloudwanderstudios.com/](https://huntprotocol.cloudwanderstudios.com/)
